rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, synthetic validation at three village samplings (found and fixed three biases), 16 per-period folders, cross-period synthesis, scorecard, operator API (gauge.py) with self-test, confirmatory script written and dry-run. Holdout not run; embedding swap and situational chi not done.
rationale.faithfulness: Period-level linear response beats its nulls in two channels (G51 nudge->activity; human->content in 6/8 periods, transfers across regimes), with validated estimators. HH116's core claim (a daily-varying, aging susceptibility) is not supported: rival R1 (constant chi) wins at day scale; P3 and P8 failed; nudge activity is resolved in one period only and its level is specification-sensitive. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E0 F1 G1 H1 I1; no holdout.
rationale.usefulness: Computable from any swarm's logs (gauge.py), and it yields near-actionable rules: the first nudge works and repeats don't; don't nudge into swarm-wide lulls; nudges don't spread to room-mates; name the agent and add new content to steer what it writes. Also a methods warning about H04's isolation bias. The daily gauge itself is not usable, which caps it below a validated monitor.

one_line: A period-level chi_op exists (nudges add ~1 active min for their target, first nudges only; human messages steer content +0.03), but the daily steerability gauge is noise.

v2.claim: A period-level χ_op exists (first nudges, human content pull); no daily steerability gauge
